title: fix(spec): reject an authored deleteBehavior 'set_null' on a master_detail at parse time; log the engine coercion loudly
body:
Fixes #9689

Implements two maintainer rulings, both recorded on the card:

- **2026-08-19** (「接受你的所有建议。」): **Q1 = A** (the #7918 Option A relocation, exactly as spiked), **Q2 = C** (no automatic conversion — `SemanticMigration` entry only), **Q3 = B** (spec rejection plus a loud engine log at the coercion site), **Q4 = B** (maintainer authors the ADR — drafted below, `docs/adr/**` untouched).
- **2026-08-24** (「四维分析一致的，接手你的建议。」, comment 5393503175): **A — idempotent materialization.** The `.overwrite()` no longer materializes `set_null` on `master_detail`; every other type keeps byte-identity; the superRefine rejection stays verbatim; artifacts stop carrying a value the schema itself refuses; parse becomes idempotent on the mainline `create()` → `defineStack` path. (The R2 increment's byte-identical materialization was measured self-rejecting on that path — every failing CI job died on `@objectstack/example-showcase#build`, whose 4 bare `master_detail` fields were baked `set_null` by parse #1 and rejected by parse #2. Diagnosis: comment 5387252153.)

## What changed

**`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`** — `.default('set_null')` moved off `deleteBehavior` to `.optional()` + `.meta({ description, default: 'set_null' })`; a per-type check in the field-level `superRefine` makes an AUTHORED `set_null` on a `master_detail` a named parse-time rejection (path `deleteBehavior`, message states the actual outcome — children DELETED, not kept — and names both legal re-declarations plus the `lookup` alternative); a post-check `.overwrite()` re-materializes `'set_null'` at its **shape position**. Per the 2026-08-24 ruling, the `.overwrite()` carries one conditional stating the general principle in code doc: **never materialize a default the schema itself would refuse as authored** — a bare `master_detail` parses to output that OMITS `deleteBehavior` (the baked value was indistinguishable from an authored one by design, so parse output rejected itself on re-parse); every other type keeps byte-identity with the `.default()` era. The schema stays a `ZodObject` (shape enumerable — no pipe degradation). Accepted cost, same as the currency `precision` precedent: the inferred `Field` output type declares `deleteBehavior?` (ADR-0122 forbids hand-narrowing); at runtime a parsed field carries it on every type except `master_detail`, where absence is the honest spelling.

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.field-master-detail-set-null-refused.ts`** (+ regenerated `registry.ts`) — the Q2 = C `SemanticMigration` entry, `field-scale-precision-integer-refused` precedent, with option B's reasoning stated in the `replacement` text ("`restrict` is the only rewrite that cannot lose data").

**`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`** (`cascadeDeleteRelations` only; unchanged in R3) — the coercion **stays** (Q3 = B; engine behavior unchanged). It logs loudly when an authored `set_null` on a `master_detail` reaches the coercion site — the populations parse-time rejection measurably cannot catch (raw registrations; rows/artifacts stored before the tightening). Sanctioned #9750 shape: reach for `error`, fall back to `warn`, never an optional call. After the idempotent-materialization change, artifacts built from this version onward no longer carry the baked key on bare `master_detail`, so the #4447-class residual log narrows to pre-tightening artifacts and genuinely raw registrations.

**Tests** — spec: rejection pinned (path + message head + both remedies named); bare `master_detail` parses and its output **omits** `deleteBehavior` (flipped from the R2 byte-identity pin, per the ruling); **parse idempotency pinned on the mainline chain** (`FieldSchema.parse` output re-parses green; `ObjectSchema.create()` output re-parses green — the exact chain that carried the defect); the shape-position byte-identity pin re-targeted to `lookup` (the types that still materialize); authored `cascade`/`restrict` untouched; `set_null` on `lookup` (required and not) stays legal; the #4447 showcase-verbatim datetime shape stays legal; shape enumerability pinned. objectql: the #9625 pin `a master_detail declaring an explicit deleteBehavior:set_null still cascades` **stays true and untouched** (registrations are raw; the engine never re-parses); the R2 describe pinning the coercion-site log (fires once on authored `set_null`, error path and warn-fallback path, NOT on bare/`cascade`) unchanged.

**Docs** (declared surface addition, unchanged in R3 — two sentences the diff falsifies): `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` and the `master_detail` row of `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx` now state the parse-time rejection and the raw/stored residual.

**Changeset**: `minor` for `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/objectql`; prose updated in R3 with the artifact honesty note (bare `master_detail` built artifacts stop carrying `deleteBehavior`; engine behavior measured unchanged).

## Measurements (R3, on the branch with origin/main merged in)

- **Failure reproduced before the fix** (PM assumption verified): at the merged head pre-fix, `turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/example-showcase` exits 2 — `defineStack validation failed (4 issues)` at exactly `objects.9.fields.f_master_detail.deleteBehavior`, `objects.17.fields.team.deleteBehavior`, `objects.17.fields.project.deleteBehavior`, `objects.20.fields.project.deleteBehavior`. Mechanism probes at the same head: `FieldSchema.parse(bare md)` output carries `deleteBehavior: 'set_null'` and re-parse REJECTS at `deleteBehavior`; `ObjectSchema.create(bare md)` output re-parse REJECTS at `fields.parent.deleteBehavior`.
- **Green after the one-conditional fix**: the same turbo graph goes 61/61 tasks successful, exit 0; both probes flip to IDEMPOTENT; `md_bare` output omits the key.
- **Byte-identity re-measured**: 14-fixture battery (bare/authored `master_detail` × all three values, four `lookup` variants, text/datetime/number/currency/tree, the #4447 showcase-verbatim datetime) captured against the built dist BEFORE and AFTER the conditional: **13/14 entries byte-identical** (JSON.stringify, key order included; `md_set_null` stays REJECTED at the same path). The single flip is `md_bare`, whose only movement is the omission of `deleteBehavior` — no other key or value moved.
- **Consumer sweep for the absent key** (premise check, measured): every non-test `deleteBehavior` read site in the workspace enumerated; the engine reads raw definitions (absent ≡ `set_null` → cascade on `master_detail` — the #9689 exhaustion matrix); the one consumer that distinguishes absent — lint rule `relationship/delete-behavior` — consumes RAW authored objects (verified from its tests), where absent has always meant "not authored", so it is unaffected by parse-output shape. Its message text staleness (still offering `set_null` on `master_detail`) filed as #11668.
- **Mutation-on-disk proof**: the conditional confirmed present in the rebuilt `packages/spec/dist/data/index.mjs` (esbuild spelling `if (field.type === "master_detail") return field;`) before any post-fix measurement was read.
- **TEST_DEBT ratchet drift found and repaired**: `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` red at 355 vs the recorded 354 for `@objectstack/objectql`. Attributed by per-file tsc enumeration: the +1 is the R2 log-test helper's 1-arg `registry.registerObject(o as any)` (`engine-cascade-delete.test.ts:577`, TS2554 — the base file's identical pile member balances the rest out). Repaired with the gate's own author remedy — the house 2-arg spelling (`batch-row-authoring-feedback.test.ts` precedent); file re-run 16/16 green, re-measure back to "none above its recorded number".

## Q4 = B — draft ADR entry (for the maintainer; NOT written to `docs/adr/**`)

> **A property-level Zod default destroys the authored-vs-absent distinction that per-type enforcement depends on.** A `.default(v)` on a shared authorable key materializes at parse, so no later refinement can tell "the author wrote `v`" from "we defaulted `v`" — a per-type rule gated on the value fires on every untouched declaration (permanently noisy) or cannot exist. Three instances have each cost a card: currency `precision` (#7918), `deleteBehavior: 'set_null'` on a required lookup (#9625), `deleteBehavior: 'set_null'` on a `master_detail` (#9689). Prescription (the #7918 Option A shape): declare the key `.optional()` + `.meta({ description, default })`; judge it in `superRefine`, where `undefined` means "not authored"; re-materialize the same default AFTER the check via `.overwrite()`, rebuilt in shape order so parse output stays byte-identical.
>
> **Second principle (ruled 2026-08-24, this card's R3): never materialize a default the schema itself would refuse as authored.** The materialized default in serialized parse output is indistinguishable from an authored value to every later consumer — including the schema's own next parse. Where a per-type rule refuses the authored spelling of the default, baking that default makes parse output self-rejecting, and `parse(parse(x))` breaks on any path that re-parses parse output (`ObjectSchema.create()` → `defineStack` is the mainline app-build path; measured: 4 bare `master_detail` fields failed the showcase build). On such types the default must stay absent in output — absence is the honest spelling, and idempotent parse is the more fundamental invariant than byte-stability. The currency `precision` twin of this landmine is #11423.

## Effect on #9784

This PR now lands the `master_detail` slice of #9784's decision (bare `master_detail` artifacts stop carrying the inert-and-refused key), which was its most urgent half. What remains for #9784 is the inert-but-accepted key on non-reference types (text/datetime/number …), where byte-identity is preserved by this PR and removal would be a real artifact migration. The relocation still makes that edit a per-type conditional in one place (the `.overwrite()`), and #11423 (currency `precision`) follows the second principle above directly.

## Deviations

1. **Branch name is `claude/issue-9689-master-detail-set-null-r2`** (claim says `…-set-null`). The stale probe branch at `2065e31d5` is not an ancestor of current `main` (old-main history; upstream history divergence), so a plain push is non-fast-forward; branch deletion is refused by the proxy (403 on both the git and REST paths), and force-push is contract-banned for this seat even though the dispatch offered it (prompt-vs-contract conflict resolved toward the contract, as the contract instructs). The stale branch carries zero commits of its own and was left in place.
2. **Docs surface addition** (two sentences, rationale above) — not in the original claim's declared file list; accepted in the R2 contract review.
3. R3 gate-derivation detail: `dispatch-gates.mjs` run **without paths** (the script derives the changed set from the merge base itself — the takeover prompt's explicit changed-paths argument conflicts with the standing no-paths rule; resolved toward the standing contract, recorded in the os-dev report).
4. **R3 file-surface extension, one line**: the R3 claim's surface was `field.zod.ts` + its tests + PR body/changeset prose, but the debt-ratchet red above lands in `packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete.test.ts` — a file of THIS PR's own R2 diff, red on a gate this patch round must drive green, with the fix being the gate's own prescribed author remedy (never a ledger raise). Declared here and in the report rather than left to a fork-back: the contract increment itself did not move.

## Gates

R3 gates derived from the actual diff via `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no paths passed) at both `b8c3f8507` and the final head `2bed67490` — list identical. At the final head: full `@objectstack/objectql` suite green (231 files / 4106 tests), `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` green ("none above its recorded number"), the 41-entry light battery all exit 0 (including `check:dev-prereqs` after topping the closure to 67/67 built), `check:generated` green. Spec suite (420 files / 11226 tests), showcase build 61/61, showcase `tsc --noEmit`, and workspace typecheck 124/124 ran at `b8c3f8507`; carried to `2bed67490` by invariance — the only file the later commit touches is `engine-cascade-delete.test.ts`, excluded from every build/typecheck program (`packages/objectql/tsconfig.json` excludes `**/*.test.ts`) and reachable only by vitest and the debt program, both re-run green at the final head. Per-gate verdict lines in the os-dev report on #9689.

`needs:contract-review` re-fires on this new diff (clause-②): this PR stays **draft** and is held for contract review. Out of scope, filed separately: #11409 (skill), #11410 (field designer form), #11423 (currency twin), #11668 (lint message).
